properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 21 at 2:10AM MST until October 21 at 2:30AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 210 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 9 miles northeast of
Wickenburg Ranch, or 29 miles west of Black Canyon City, moving north
at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Yarnell, Peeples Valley, Stanton, Wagoner and Hassayampa River
Canyon Wilderness.

This includes State Route 89 between mile markers 275 and 282.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.areaDesc: Ocracoke Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 21 at 4:11AM EDT until October 21 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, up to 2 to 4 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous
rip currents, large breaking waves expected, and strong
longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this
morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. This could be life threatening if
you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore currents will
create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant ocean overwash impacts are
expected at vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high
tide cycles into mid week. Minor soundside water level rises
will also be possible today.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: East Carteret
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 21 at 4:11AM EDT until October 21 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves
expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Core Banks beaches.

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw
a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck
and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 9:45 AM today.
properties.instruction:
Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 21 at 2:06AM MDT until October 23 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of western, central, and north-central New Mexico,
mainly along and west of the Continental Divide.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A potent Pacific storm system will draw up anomalously high
moisture into the Desert Southwest, generating repeated rounds of
widespread showers and thunderstorms. Fast moving thunderstorms
producing locally heavy rainfall will have the ability to pass
over the same areas repeatedly, threatening flash flooding.
Rainfall amounts through late Thursday night will generally range
from 0.75 inch to 1.5 inch in most areas, with locally higher
totals up to 3 inches.
- This includes Farmington, Gallup, Zuni Pueblo, and portions of
Navajo Nation.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Lucie, and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

properties.instruction:

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 21 at 4:00AM AST until October 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Exposed northwesterly and north-facing beaches of
Puerto Rico, Culebra, and the northern US Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 21 at 2:39AM EDT until October 21 at 10:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Cape May, Atlantic Coastal Cape May,
Coastal Atlantic, Coastal Ocean and Southeastern Burlington.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional elevated high tide cycles beyond
this evening are expected.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 10:11PM MDT until October 23 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country and San Rafael Swell.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A late season surge of tropical moisture will bring widespread
moderate to at times heavy rainfall across much of eastern Utah
beginning Wednesday afternoon, and continuing through Thursday.
Local rainfall totals in excess of 2 inches are expected through
Thursday evening.
- All normally dry washes, small streams and mainstem rivers will
see elevated flows from this excessive rainfall, with periods of
heavier rainfall resulting in flash flooding. Backcountry roads
may become impassable due to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

People in the backcountry should ensure they have alternative routes
available in case their primary route becomes impassable.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 8:34PM PDT until October 22 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall from storms
training over the same area.

* WHERE...A portion of central California, including the following
areas, Bakersfield, Buena Vista, Buttonwillow - Lost Hills - I5,
Frazier Mountain Communities, Grapevine, Indian Wells Valley, Kern
River Valley, Mojave Desert, Mojave Desert Slopes, Piute Walker
Basin, South End San Joaquin Valley, Tehachapi and West Side
Mountains South of 198.

* WHEN...From 8 AM PDT Wednesday through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become
clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong area of low pressure off the Southern California coast
will move inland and interact with tropical moisture.
- Be especially careful on Highway 58 between mile markers 101 to
103 and the Borel burn scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued October 20 at 9:52PM EDT until October 22 at 11:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 9 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Statement,
isolated minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Statement, from 3 AM EDT Wednesday through
Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding is expected around
high tide.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 20 at 9:12PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end of this
week. There is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage
next week after northeasterly winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.5 feet early this
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon EDT.

* WHAT...Coastal flooding and high surf conditions are possible
due to 40 to 60 mph winds.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk and
Kwigillingok.

* WHEN...8 AM Friday through 1 AM Saturday, particularly around
high tides near 10 AM and 10 PM Friday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely scenario is for water
levels to be 2 to 3 ft above the average high tide line, which
would be similar to the water levels during the August 18 2024
storm. This will likely be the strongest storm of the 2026
season so far. We will be closely monitoring this storm. In the
meantime, please have a plan in place.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be
alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to
protect property.

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued October 20 at 3:07PM AKDT until October 25 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding possible. Water levels in
the 4 to 8 feet above the normal high tide range for Hooper Bay.
Water levels in the 2 to 6 foot above the normal high tide range
for the rest of the Yukon Delta.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHEN...From late Thursday night through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Low lying property including homes, businesses, and
some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline
erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strong south to southeast winds up to 65
mph possible. 8 feet at Hooper Bay is the current high end
forecast estimate with 6 feet being the current mean forecast
estimate. There remains considerable uncertainty in the exact
height of the highest water levels and we will continue to
update the forecast as confidence improves.
properties.instruction:
Travel may be difficult. Take the necessary actions to protect
flood- prone property.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 12:37AM MST until October 22 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An upper-level trough will bring a deep surge of subtropical and
tropical moisture into our region. Showers and thunderstorms will
develop across much of northern and central Arizona early
Wednesday morning and continue through Thursday evening. Stronger
thunderstorms will bring threats of Flash Flooding, while more
prolonged rainfall could lead to elevated flow in streams,
rivers, and washes.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 19 at 12:31PM PDT until October 23 at 3:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf of 3 to 6 feet expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion and tidal overflows may
occur across south-facing beaches especially along the Malibu
Coast and in the Long Beach area.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
